ov: Small, nocturnal hopping rodents of the hot deserts of North Africa and Asia, with very long back legs, a tuft-tipped tail longer than the body, and often huge ears. They move almost entirely on two legs, zigzagging and leaping to escape predators.

why.h: It digs a special winter burrow to hibernate in, longer and deeper than its summer one.

rg: Hot deserts across North Africa and Asia.
df: Mostly plants and soft seeds, plus insects; some species eat other small animals.
fx: Normally hops 10–13 cm, but can leap up to 3 m when a predator is after it.
Unlike almost any mammal apart from humans, it moves only on two legs, even at slow speeds.
